bibl.title: Building a Conceptual Framework: Philosophy, Definitions, and Procedure

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the conceptual framework itself - what a concept is, what a network of concepts is, and how one is built from a multidisciplinary literature
span.quote: Current usage of the terms conceptual framework and theoretical framework are vague and imprecise. In this paper I define conceptual framework as a network, or “a plane,” of interlinked concepts that together provide a comprehensive understanding of a phenomenon or phenomena.

span.label: how can a conceptual framework for a multidisciplinary phenomenon be built systematically, when the terms `conceptual framework` and `theoretical framework` are themselves used vaguely
span.quote: Despite the extensive literature that provides logical guidelines for qualitatively deriving theories from text and data (Glaser & Strauss, 1967; Harris, 2003; Miles & Huberman, 1994; Myers, 2009; Strauss & Corbin, 1990), there is a lack of a qualitative systematic method for building conceptual frameworks. This is particularly noticeable in the multidisciplinary literature.

span.label: redefines `concept`, `conceptual framework` and `conceptual framework analysis`, and gives an eight-phase procedure for building a network of concepts out of a multidisciplinary literature
span.quote: Concept has some components that define it. All concepts are characterized by a number of features: an irregular contour defined by its components; a history, some “bits” or components that come from other concepts, and elements that can be traced back to other concepts.

span.label: method
span.quote: Yet, the existing conceptual analysis technique is inadequate for theorizing the concepts that emerge from the text. Therefore, in this article I propose a new technique, which I refer to as conceptual framework analysis, as a grounded theory technique, or tactic, that aims to generate, identify, and trace a phenomenon’s major concepts, which together constitute its theoretical framework.

span.label: a term used constantly and defined loosely - `conceptual framework` and `theoretical framework` in current usage - with no systematic method for producing the thing it names
span.quote: Despite the extensive literature that provides logical guidelines for qualitatively deriving theories from text and data (Glaser & Strauss, 1967; Harris, 2003; Miles & Huberman, 1994; Myers, 2009; Strauss & Corbin, 1990), there is a lack of a qualitative systematic method for building conceptual frameworks. This is particularly noticeable in the multidisciplinary literature.

span.label: conceptual analysis by grounded theory over a multidisciplinary literature, in eight named phases, demonstrated on sustainable development
span.term: conceptual analysis by grounded theory over a multidisciplinary literature, in eight named phases, demonstrated on sustainable development
span.quote: The aim of this phase is to deconstruct each concept; to identify its main attributes, characteristics, assumptions, and role; and, subsequently, to organize and categorize the concepts according to their features and ontological, epistemological, and methodological role. The result of this phase is a table that includes four columns. The first includes the names of the concepts; the second includes a description of each concept; the third categorizes each concept according to its ontological, epistemological, or methodological role; and the fourth presents the references for each concept.

span.label: **A CONCEPT IS DEFINED BY ITS COMPONENTS, AND CARRIES PIECES OF OTHER CONCEPTS.** `Every concept usually contains BITS OR COMPONENTS ORIGINATING FROM OTHER CONCEPTS` and `ALL CONCEPTS RELATE BACK TO OTHER CONCEPTS`
span.quote: 2. Every concept has a history. 3. Every concept usually contains “bits” or components originating from other concepts. 4. All concepts relate back to other concepts. 5. A concept is always created by something (and cannot be created from nothing).

span.label: and it is historical: `EVERY CONCEPT HAS A HISTORY` - which is why a concept must be understood `relative to its own components, to other concepts, to the plane on which it is defined, AND TO THE PROBLEM IT IS SUPPOSED TO RESOLVE`
span.quote: When defining of the term concept, I follow and adapt the approach of Deleuze and Guattari in their What Is Philosophy? (1991), in which they hold that “every concept has components and is defined by them” (p. 15). These “components, or what defines the consistency of the concept; its endo-consistency; are distinct, heterogeneous and, yet, not separable” (p. 19). It is a multiplicity, but “not every multiplicity is conceptual,” and “there is no concept with only one component” (p. 15).

span.label: **A FRAMEWORK IS A NETWORK, NOT A PILE.** `A conceptual framework is NOT MERELY A COLLECTION OF CONCEPTS but, rather, a construct in which EACH CONCEPT PLAYS AN INTEGRAL ROLE`, and each plays `an ontological or epistemological role`
span.quote: A conceptual framework is not merely a collection of concepts but, rather, a construct in which each concept plays an integral role. According to Miles and Huberman (1994), a conceptual framework “lays out the key factors, constructs, or variables, and presumes relationships among them” (p. 440).

span.label: **AND THE PROCEDURE'S OUTPUT IS A TAGGED RECORD WITH ITS SOURCES.** Phase 4 produces `a table that includes FOUR COLUMNS. The first includes the NAMES of the concepts; the second includes a DESCRIPTION of each concept; the third CATEGORIZES each concept according to its ontological, epistemological, or methodological ROLE; and the fourth presents THE REFERENCES FOR EACH CONCEPT`
span.quote: The aim of this phase is to deconstruct each concept; to identify its main attributes, characteristics, assumptions, and role; and, subsequently, to organize and categorize the concepts according to their features and ontological, epistemological, and methodological role. The result of this phase is a table that includes four columns. The first includes the names of the concepts; the second includes a description of each concept; the third categorizes each concept according to its ontological, epistemological, or methodological role; and the fourth presents the references for each concept.

span.label: the phase before it expects disagreement rather than avoiding it: the result of identifying and naming concepts is `A LIST OF NUMEROUS COMPETING AND SOMETIMES CONTRADICTORY CONCEPTS`
span.quote: The aim in this phase is to read and reread the selected data and “discover” concepts (Glaser & Strauss. 1967; Strauss & Corbin. 1990). Its result is a list of numerous competing and sometimes contradictory concepts.

span.label: **COUNTING A TERM IS NOT THEORIZING WITH IT.** Existing conceptual analysis chooses a concept and `the analysis involves, among other things, QUANTIFYING AND TALLYING ITS PRESENCE` - and Carley: `the focus on concepts implicit to traditional content analysis often results in AN OVERESTIMATION OF THE SIMILARITY OF TEXTS BECAUSE MEANING IS NEGLECTED`
span.quote: In the existing techniques of conceptual analysis, “a concept is chosen for examination, and the analysis involves, among other things, quantifying and tallying its presence” (Palmquist, Carley, & Dale, 1997; see also Finney & Corbett, 2007).

span.label: **THE FRAMEWORK IS EXPECTED TO CHANGE, AND THAT IS A PROPERTY NOT A DEFECT** - `A theory or a theoretical framework representing a multidisciplinary phenomenon WILL ALWAYS BE DYNAMIC and may be revised according to new insights, comments, literature`
span.quote: A theory or a theoretical framework representing a multidisciplinary phenomenon will always be dynamic and may be revised according to new insights, comments, literature, and so on.

span.label: and validation is social rather than statistical: `Validating a theoretical framework is a process that STARTS WITH THE RESEARCHER, WHO THEN SEEKS VALIDATION AMONG OUTSIDERS`
span.quote: The question is whether the proposed framework and its concepts make sense not only to the researcher but also to other scholars and practitioners. Does the framework present a reasonable theory for scholars studying the phenomenon from different disciplines? Validating a theoretical framework is a process that starts with the researcher, who then seeks validation among “outsiders.”

span.label: **THE PAPER NAMES THIS PROJECT'S OWN INTER-RATER RISK AS ITS OWN LIMITATION** - `DIFFERENT RESEARCHERS MAY HAVE DIFFERENT CONCEPTIONS OF THE SAME PHENOMENON AND MAY CREATE DIFFERENT PLANES AND CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORKS`, along with `possible difficulties finding suitable texts and data`
span.quote: Although conceptual framework analysis certainly has its limitations - such as the fact that different researchers may have different conceptions of the same phenomenon and may create different “planes” and conceptual frameworks, and possible difficulties finding suitable texts and data - it also offers some important advantages.

span.label: and the method declares that it cannot predict: `Conceptual frameworks are INDETERMINIST in nature and therefore DO NOT ENABLE US TO PREDICT AN OUTCOME` - stated as a design choice, which also means no failed prediction can falsify one
span.quote: 5. Conceptual frameworks are indeterminist in nature and therefore do not enable us to predict an outcome. Levering (2002) has suggested that “the idea that human behavior can be explained and predicted is roughly based on the concept of external factors being caught in an accidental cohesion, and the idea that human actions can be understood, but not predicted, is based on the concept of freedom” (p. 38).

span.label: **the validation criterion is whether it makes sense to other scholars** - `The question is whether the proposed framework and its concepts MAKE SENSE not only to the researcher but also to other scholars and practitioners`, with a conference presentation named as the venue. There is no measure and no threshold
span.quote: The question is whether the proposed framework and its concepts make sense not only to the researcher but also to other scholars and practitioners. Does the framework present a reasonable theory for scholars studying the phenomenon from different disciplines? Validating a theoretical framework is a process that starts with the researcher, who then seeks validation among “outsiders.”

span.label: the integration phase reduces the concept count by judgement - `integrate and group together concepts that have similarities to one new concept. This phase REDUCES THE NUMBER OF CONCEPTS DRASTICALLY and allows us to MANIPULATE TO A REASONABLE NUMBER` - with `reasonable` undefined
span.quote: The aim in this phase is to integrate and group together concepts that have similarities to one new concept. This phase reduces the number of concepts drastically and allows us to manipulate to a reasonable number of concepts.

span.label: **and the demonstration case is one the paper itself calls unsettled** - existing definitions of sustainable development are `vague`, `devoid of operative definitions`, `fraught with contradictions`, and authors `are NOT EVEN IN AGREEMENT ON WHAT IT IS THAT NEEDS TO BE SUSTAINED`
span.quote: Some have argued that the existing definitions of sustainable development are vague (Gow, 1992; Mozaffar, 2001), devoid of operative definitions (Villanueva, 1997), and fraught with contradictions (Redclift, 1987), and that the topic itself is confused (Berke & Conroy, 2000; Redclift, 1994). Others have pointed out that authors on the subject employ unclear symbolic rhetoric (Andrews, 1997; Solow, 1992) and are not even in agreement on what it is that needs to be sustained

span.label: conceptual framework analysis is built as a procedure of theorization on the grounded theory method
span.quote: Conceptual framework analysis offers a procedure of theorization for building conceptual frameworks based on grounded theory method.

span.label: requiring the framework to be validated by outsiders - scholars and practitioners from the disciplines it draws on, not only by its author

span.quote: Current usage of the terms conceptual framework and theoretical framework are vague and imprecise. In this paper I define conceptual framework as a network, or “a plane,” of interlinked concepts that together provide a comprehensive understanding of a phenomenon or phenomena.

span.label: conceptual framework analysis - a grounded theory technique `that aims to generate, identify, and trace a phenomenon's major concepts, which together constitute its theoretical framework`
span.term: conceptual framework analysis - a grounded theory technique `that aims to generate, identify, and trace a phenomenon's major concepts, which together constitute its theoretical framework`
span.quote: Yet, the existing conceptual analysis technique is inadequate for theorizing the concepts that emerge from the text. Therefore, in this article I propose a new technique, which I refer to as conceptual framework analysis, as a grounded theory technique, or tactic, that aims to generate, identify, and trace a phenomenon’s major concepts, which together constitute its theoretical framework.

span.label: model - the term reserved for a construct based on variables or factors, so that `conceptual framework` can be reserved for one based on concepts alone
span.term: model - the term reserved for a construct based on variables or factors, so that `conceptual framework` can be reserved for one based on concepts alone
span.quote: To discourage loose usage of the term conceptual framework, I propose basing conceptual frameworks not on variable or factors but on concepts alone. When variables or factors are used, I suggest employing the term model.

span.label: phases in the procedure
span.term: phases in the procedure
span.quote: A theory or a theoretical framework representing a multidisciplinary phenomenon will always be dynamic and may be revised according to new insights, comments, literature, and so on.

span.label: concepts in the sustainable development framework
span.term: concepts in the sustainable development framework
span.quote: The conceptual analysis undertaken along the lines laid down in the first part of this article identified seven distinct concepts that make up the theoretical world of sustainability (Jabareen, 2008).

span.label: Validation is `whether the proposed framework and its concepts MAKE SENSE not only to the researcher but also to other scholars`, sought by presenting at a conference or seminar. **There is no coefficient, no threshold and no inter-rater statistic anywhere in the procedure** - and the paper's own limitation is that different researchers will build different planes. The two sentences belong together.
span.term: **a method with no measure, stated as such**
span.quote: The question is whether the proposed framework and its concepts make sense not only to the researcher but also to other scholars and practitioners. Does the framework present a reasonable theory for scholars studying the phenomenon from different disciplines? Validating a theoretical framework is a process that starts with the researcher, who then seeks validation among “outsiders.”

span.label: each concept's role in the framework - ontological, epistemological or methodological. The paper makes this a column of the output table, not a judgement left implicit
span.term: each concept's role in the framework - ontological, epistemological or methodological. The paper makes this a column of the output table, not a judgement left implicit
span.quote: The concepts that constitute a conceptual framework support one another, articulate their respective phenomena, and establish a framework-specific philosophy. Conceptual frameworks possess ontological, epistemological, and methodological assumptions, and each concept within a conceptual framework plays an ontological or epistemological role.
